implementation_notes: JavaScript needs no message class at all: a document is an object literal, JSON is a subset of the syntax, JSON.stringify(doc) produces the wire form and JSON.parse(body) returns the document the receiver inspects, with optional replacer and reviver hooks for values JSON cannot express. What the language does not give you is validation or typing, so at a trust boundary the document is checked with a schema validator (zod, ajv) or hand-written guards, and structuredClone is the in-process way to hand a document on without sharing mutable state. Node's Buffer and streams carry large bodies, and the pattern's own answer to a document that is too big is a claim check rather than a bigger message.
pitfalls: JSON.parse throws SyntaxError on malformed input, so an unguarded parse turns one bad document into a crashed consumer.
Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles: identifiers beyond 2^53 are silently rounded unless they travel as strings and are revived explicitly.
undefined, functions and symbols disappear from JSON.stringify output, and Date/Map/Set need replacer/reviver discipline to survive a round trip.
A __proto__ key in parsed input can pollute prototypes when the document is merged into other objects instead of being read field by field.
